name: Castello di Semivicoli
address: Via San Nicola, 4, 66010 Casacanditella CH, Italy
architectural_style: 17th-18th century baronial palace built for the Perticone barons; acquired in 2004 by the Masciarelli winery family, restored, and reopened as a hotel in 2009
visit_duration: Overnight stay; winery tastings and cellar tours are separately open to the public
best_season: Year-round; September to October for the grape harvest
accessibility: All 11 rooms are within the historic palace; contact the hotel directly regarding specific accessibility requirements.
tagline: A 17th-century baronial palace turned 11-room hotel by the Masciarelli winery family, with rooms named for the estate's former granary and prison cells
highlights: Owned by the Masciarelli family, one of Abruzzo's most recognized wineries (Trebbiano, Montepulciano d'Abruzzo)
Only 11 rooms — one of the most intimate properties in this entire collection
Themed rooms that preserve the historic function of the space (granary, prison cells)
description:
Castello di Semivicoli is in fact a baronial palace built between the 17th and 18th centuries for the Perticone barons, in the hills of Casacanditella, at the heart of Abruzzo's wine country. For generations it functioned as a noble residence and administrative center for the surrounding agricultural land, incorporating outbuildings such as a granary and a domestic prison, typical of large Italian rural estates of the Ancien Régime.

In 2004 the property was acquired by the Masciarelli family, one of the most influential wineries in the international rediscovery of Abruzzo wine since the 1980s. After a careful restoration completed in 2009, the palace reopened as an 11-room hotel, integrated into the estate's wine production: guests sleep literally among the vineyards that supply the Masciarelli winery.

The palace's granary and prison outbuildings, typical features of a self-sufficient noble rural estate, now lend their names and character to two of the hotel's suites — the Suite Granaio and the Suite Segrete — giving guests a tangible link to the building's working agricultural and administrative past rather than a purely decorative historic theme.

The Masciarelli family's stewardship since 2004 connects the property directly to Abruzzo's broader wine renaissance, in which a handful of committed producers raised the region's international profile considerably from the 1980s onward.

With only 11 rooms, Semivicoli offers a genuinely intimate scale rarely found among the larger resort-style castle-hotels in this collection, with the wine estate's own vineyards forming the immediate surroundings rather than a separate attraction.
history: Castello di Semivicoli is a baronial palace built in the 17th-18th centuries for the Perticone barons in the hills of Casacanditella, Abruzzo. In 2004 it was acquired by the Masciarelli winery family and, after a restoration completed in 2009, reopened as an 11-room hotel integrated into the estate's wine production. Rooms preserve the palace's original functions in their names, including the Suite Granaio (former granary) and the Suite Segrete (former prison cells).

faqs.question: Can I visit the Masciarelli winery at Castello di Semivicoli without staying overnight?
faqs.answer: Yes — tastings and tours of the Masciarelli winery are open to the public, with or without a room booking.

faqs.question: How many rooms does Castello di Semivicoli have?
faqs.answer: Just 11, all within the historic 17th-18th century palace — among the most intimate properties in this collection.

faqs.question: What are the Suite Granaio and Suite Segrete?
faqs.answer: Two of the hotel's themed suites, occupying the palace's former granary (Granaio) and former prison cells (Segrete) respectively.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** About 15 minutes from Chieti and 20 minutes from Pescara by car; Pescara's Abruzzo Airport (PSR) is about 25 minutes away.

**Rooms & rates:** Just 11 rooms, all within the historic palace — the Suite Granaio (former granary) and Suite Segrete (former prison cells) are the most distinctive. From €154/night.

**On-site:** Masciarelli winery with tastings and guided tours, outdoor pool, restaurant serving the estate's own wine and olive oil.

**Good to know:** With only 11 rooms, book ahead for the harvest season (September-October), when the winery's activity is at its peak.

**Combine with:** Chieti (archaeological sites, ~15 min), the Costa dei Trabocchi coastline, and Maiella National Park.
